​Ghaas Phoos manages to strike a balance between an "upmarket" feel and the relaxed, airy charm Goa is known for. With an open-air setup surrounded by vibrant bougainvillea, it feels like a hidden garden oasis. It’s spacious enough for large families but intimate enough for a quiet dinner. Unlike many beachside shacks, the presentation here is polished, making it feel more like a boutique dining destination.
​The Menu: Beyond the Basics
​The menu is 100% vegetarian, with a strong emphasis on fusion and high-quality ingredients.
​Indian Classics: They do the staples exceptionally well—the Malai Kofta and Dal Tadka are crowd favorites.
​Goan Flavors: For those wanting a local taste without the meat, their Vegetable Xacuti is a must-try, capturing the complex spice profile of Goa perfectly.
​Global Options: They offer a variety of thin-crust pizzas, pastas, and Asian dishes.
​Vegan & Jain Friendly: They are incredibly accommodating; most paneer dishes can be swapped for tofu, and they offer specific Jain preparations upon request.
​Standout Features
​The Bar: Having a full bar license in a pure-veg establishment is a huge plus. You can pair your meal with a chilled beer or a well-crafted cocktail, which isn't always common in traditional veg spots.
​Service: The staff is frequently praised for being attentive and warm (shoutout to Mahesh, who many regulars mention by name).
​Presentation: They don't just "serve" food; they plate it with an artistic touch that elevates the entire experience.
​Things to Note
​Price Point: It is slightly pricier than your average local eatery or beach shack, but the quality of ingredients and the ambiance justify the cost.
​Parking: As with many spots near Benaulim beach, parking can get a bit tight during peak dinner hours.
​The Verdict
​Whether you’re a lifelong vegetarian or just looking for a break from heavy seafood, Ghaas Phoos is one of the best pure-veg spots in South Goa. First-timers: it's tucked behind the HDFC bank on Colva Beach Road. The turn leads into a narrow lane, so go slow and honk. You'll hit their spacious parking lot in under a minute.

Now, the food. We ordered a feast and the portions were massive. Everything was cooked with serious care.

Started with a Fresh Lime Soda and Piña Colada—simple, perfect. The Chicken and Egg Salad was our first "wow" moment. Tender chicken, rich, delicious.

Starters were incredible: Chicken Crispy, Bombil Fry, Chicken Teriyaki. Zabbardast is the only word that fits.

For mains, the Paneer Makhanwala was a dream. Soft, fresh paneer with gravy we wiped clean with fluffy chapatis. The prawns curry and Thai curry? Soul food. We went quiet and just ate.

Dessert: caramel pudding with ice cream was heavenly. But the Scotch Ice cream? I told my friend it's the only reason I'd need to be reincarnated.

We were the last table there, which gave us time to chat with the friendly staff and soak in the peaceful vibe. The owner, Pawan, has clearly poured his heart into this place and created a fantastic experience without the crazy price tag you'd expect.

Now, the food. We ordered a feast and the portions were massive. Everything was cooked with serious care.

Started with a Fresh Lime Soda and Piña Colada—simple, perfect. The Chicken and Egg Salad was our first "wow" moment. Tender chicken, rich, delicious.

Starters were incredible: Chicken Crispy, Bombil Fry, Chicken Teriyaki. Zabbardast is the only word that fits.

The highlight of the evening was undoubtedly the food. The ingredients tasted authentic and it was evident that great care had been taken to stay true to Italian flavours. Having travelled to Italy several times, I can honestly say that the cuisine was genuinely authentic and delicious. The dishes were well prepared, flavourful, and among the better Italian meals I have enjoyed in Goa.
However, the overall dining experience did not quite match the premium pricing. The restaurant was extremely hot and humid during our visit. The dining area relied solely on fans, which unfortunately circulated warm air rather than providing relief. For a restaurant offering fine-dining style Italian cuisine at these price levels, an air-conditioned section would greatly enhance guest comfort.
The staff were courteous, hardworking, and clearly trying to do their best, but they appeared stretched due to the number of tables being served. As a result, service was slower than expected. Even a simple request for ice cubes required a follow-up and a wait before it arrived. At one point, we were also presented with another table's bill, suggesting that the team was struggling to keep up during a busy service.
We had pre-ordered a tiramisu when making our reservation, but after finishing our main course, we still had to wait quite some time for dessert to arrive. Sitting in the heat while waiting made the experience less enjoyable than it should have been.

Cajy’s Multicuisine Restaurant perfectly captures Goa’s relaxed charm with its warm, welcoming ambience and unhurried vibe. The space feels comfortable and inviting, making it ideal for a leisurely meal. What truly elevates the experience is the owner’s hospitality friendly and genuinely passionate about guiding guests through the restaurant’s specialities. Every dish we tried was excellent with proper local preparations.

Dish-wise highlights:
King Fish Rava Fry – Crisp on the outside and succulent inside.
Bombil Stuffed Chilli – A delightful balance of spice and texture, with the bombil adding a unique coastal character.
Pomfret Rechado – fiery recheado masala that packs flavour without overpowering the freshness of the fish.
Calamari Golden Fry – Light, crunchy batter with tender calamari.
Calamari Chilli Garlic – garlicky, and spicy.
Calamari Masala Fry – Rich, aromatic masala clinging beautifully to perfectly cooked calamari.
Kashmiri Chicken – Mildly spiced with a smooth, well-balanced thick dry gravy.
Chicken Pepper Garlic.
Pork Auzol – Goan flavours at their best.
Beef Chilli Fry – Tender beef tossed in a spicy, savoury masala.
Tongue Pepper Garlic – Exceptionally tender, with a strong pepper-garlic profile that’s both unique and memorable.
Overall Verdict:
Cajy’s is a must-visit for anyone looking to enjoy expertly cooked seafood and meat dishes in a relaxed Goan setting with beer to chill. We also had the opportunity to taste the Pork Vindaloo and Mutton Biryani, both of which were excellent and full of rich flavours. Every dish was well prepared and satisfying.

In fact, we enjoyed the food so much that we chose to have our meals there on all three days of our stay. The quality, taste, and service remained excellent throughout.

When we walked in, it was completely empty.

And that turned out to be the right call.

When the food arrived, it didn’t just look good — it delivered. Every dish was thoughtfully prepared, with flavours that felt balanced and precise. You could tell there was attention to detail in the cooking, not just presentation.

What stood out was consistency — everything we ordered hit the mark.

The pricing felt reasonable for the experience. Portions lean slightly on the smaller side, but the quality and taste more than make up for it.

The space itself was clean, comfortable, and paired with good music that added to the overall mood. The staff remained attentive without being intrusive — a balance that’s harder to find than it sounds.

Sometimes, the best meals come from places you almost walked away from.

The restaurant has a relaxed, welcoming vibe with authentic country music playing in the background, adding to its old-Goa charm. There's ample parking, making it convenient even during busy hours. The service is warm, attentive, and genuinely hospitable.

We ordered the Goan fish curry with rice, Chicken Cafreal, and a crispy fried fish. The fish curry was rich, flavourful, and perfectly balanced with coconut and spices, paired beautifully with fluffy steamed rice. The Chicken Cafreal was the star of the meal—marinated in the traditional green herb and spice paste, tender, juicy, and packed with bold, authentic flavours without being overwhelmingly spicy. The fried fish was wonderfully crisp on the outside while remaining fresh and succulent inside.

What stands out is that the food tastes homemade rather than commercial. The recipes stay true to Goan culinary traditions, using fresh ingredients and local spices. The portions are generous, and every dish feels thoughtfully prepared.

Like most restaurants in Goa, they serve beer and wine, making it easy to enjoy a leisurely meal. Another pleasant surprise was the pricing. Considering the quality, quantity, and authenticity of the food, Cota Cozinha is very reasonably priced and offers excellent value for money.

It's easy to understand why so many diners recommend this place. Regulars often praise its consistently fresh seafood, authentic Goan recipes, friendly staff, quick service, and relaxed atmosphere. After our visit, we couldn't agree more.

If you're looking to enjoy genuine Goan flavours away from the usual tourist traps, Cota Cozinha is a fantastic choice. Delicious food, warm hospitality, relaxed ambience, and pocket-friendly prices make it a place you'll want to return to.
